# Mutant schemata

64 mutants use one shared build. `mutant_active(id)` caches `NET_MUTANT` in a OnceLock. Absent or 0 selects the original code. Each test process gets a fresh switch. Mutant ids remain stable. M095 now preserves the payload and checks the full translated prefix; its run-3 reference used the earlier constant-output change. Outcome agreement below compares test names and pass/fail results, not identical mutation semantics. Function bodies are generated from the pinned copy; branches preserve every occurrence of an edit, including both formatter padding paths for M100.

The remaining mutants retain their own build because stable Rust cannot read an environment variable during const evaluation. The upstream const tests and their declarations remain unchanged. Only guarded methods and their runtime callers lose `const` in the copy; this does not test those methods as const. Each separate build has an isolated crate and target under target/separate; it leaves the shared copy unchanged. Published sources remain read-only.

Before is a measured replay of the legacy runner with the existing incremental target and warm cache, including its real-std baseline. After includes the shared upstream/copy baselines and identical mutant suites; the real-std baseline uses one additional build outside the mutation timer. These are local wall times, not a cross-machine performance guarantee. Before includes repeated restoration and separate upstream/proposed Cargo compilations.
